meta.triageRationale: One story in the plugin's chat. The review pane can already be opened on a document and brought into view; the chat host already sees every tool result of a turn and has one caller. The work is to notice, during a chat turn, that a document now awaits approval, and to ask the review pane to open it once. A few files in one module, one design choice (what the signal is), a small number of tasks. No daemon change is expected.

findings.premise: ac1/ac2: end() in a finally around the existing `await run` in startTurn runs exactly once for a turn that completed, failed, was stopped or was superseded, so the end-of-turn rule covers documents that became pending without a pendingApproval tool result.
findings.evidence: chat-panel.ts:1354-1356 is the single `const run = turns.start(s, req, sink); started(); await run;` site. turn-lifecycle.ts:242-255 start() awaits run() in try/finally; run() returns on every path: lock wait dropped (227, 235-238), aborted setup (321), detach (338), output ended (339-358), superseded terminal (365-369), terminal (375-383), and a throwing sink/adapter is caught at 386-393. The two early returns that refuse a message are chat-panel.ts:1199 and 1202, before turns.start. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/turn-lifecycle.ts]
findings.action: None. Note for the builder: a detach (window reload / chat switch, turn-lifecycle.ts:329-334) also resolves `run`, so end() fires then while the CLI keeps writing; the lazily begun followed turn takes over from its first event, as the design states.

findings.premise: ac3: when the review pane is not available the chat host gets no presenter and behaves as today.
findings.evidence: extension.ts builds the chat host (567-638) and the review host (668-703) inside the same insrc.chat.enabled block, so there is no runtime state with a chat host and no review host; with the flag off neither exists. summary.prose: When the assistant in the chat produces a document that needs your approval, the review pane now opens on that document by itself; you no longer run the review command and look for it in the table. It opens once per turn for each document, beside the chat and without taking the cursor out of the chat box. If a turn produces several documents they are opened one after another, so the last is the one on show and the others are in the pane's table. A turn that was picked up again after a window reload opens what it produces from then on; a document it wrote before the reload is in the table. Acceptance: ac1, a document a chat turn presents for approval is opened in the review pane without any action, whether a workflow tool call wrote it or it became pending some other way during the turn, for a turn the window runs and for one it picks up again; ac2, each document is opened once per turn, the chat keeps keyboard focus, and re-reads or re-renders of the pane open nothing; ac3, nothing happens when the review pane is not available, and a failure to read the pending list never disturbs the chat turn.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone Story — no parent HLD. Designed directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Dev chat: a document presented for approval is opened in the review pane automatically

api.name: createReviewPresenter
api.signature: createReviewPresenter(deps: { pendingDocuments(): Promise<readonly { id: string; mdPath: string }[]>; open(target: { artifactId: string; mdPath: string }): void; log: ChatPanelLogger }): ReviewPresenter

parameters.name: deps.pendingDocuments
parameters.purpose: The documents awaiting approval, each with its path; wired to the review client's new pendingDocuments().

parameters.name: deps.open
parameters.purpose: Opens the review pane on one document; wired to the review host's openArtifact with quiet set.

parameters.name: deps.log
parameters.purpose: Where a failed pending read or a throwing open is recorded.

returns.type: ReviewPresenter { begin(): PresentedTurn }; PresentedTurn { toolResult(output: string): void; end(): void }
returns.meaning: New module vscode-plugin/src/chat/review-presenter.ts, free of vscode. begin() starts one turn's state and returns its handle, which becomes the newest. When the previous newest handle has ended (or there is none) the state is fresh: the set of ids this turn opened is empty and `before`, the ids pending now, is read at once. When the previous newest handle has NOT ended (the user sent a message while a turn was still running), the new handle takes over that handle's `before` and its opened set instead of reading anew, so whatever the earlier turn makes pending is still new to the later one. toolResult(output): when the text contains 'pendingApproval' and parses as a JSON object whose pendingApproval.artifactPath is a non-empty string, it reads the pending list and opens the document whose mdPath EQUALS that path (both are absolute paths the daemon resolves the same way); as tolerance only, a list path that is the block's path's tail after a '/' also matches. It opens nothing when this turn already opened that id. end(): when this handle is still the newest, it reads the pending list and opens each document whose id is not in `before` and was not opened by this turn, in the list's order; when a later begin() has happened it opens nothing: the later handle carries its state on and its own end opens what is new. end() a second time does nothing. Every call of a handle is queued behind that handle's earlier calls, including the read begin() started, so a slow read cannot reorder them. Calls return at once and never throw to the caller.

errors.condition: A pending read that fails or throws, and an open that throws, are logged; nothing is opened for that call. If the read in begin() failed, `before` is unknown and end() opens nothing, while toolResult still works.

preconditions: The chat host calls begin() once per turn and end() once on its handle
postconditions: A turn opens a document at most once
A document that was pending before the turn is opened only if a tool result of the turn names it
Text that is not JSON, JSON without the block, and a path that matches no pending document open nothing
A later turn may open the same document again when it is presented again
With overlapping turns (begin A, begin B, end A, end B) A's end opens nothing and B's end opens every document that became pending since A began and was not opened yet

api.name: createChatPanelHost (deps.presenter)

parameters.name: deps.presenter
parameters.purpose: Optional. The chat host begins a presented turn for every turn it runs and for every turn it follows.

returns.meaning: RUN TURN, in startTurn: after the two early returns that refuse a message before any run, and just before turns.start, `const shown = presenter?.begin()`. In the run sink's onEvent, a 'tool-result' event whose isError is not true calls shown.toolResult(ev.output), before the existing handling and whatever that handling does with the event (held back for a diff or posted). A turn that was superseded gets no more events at its sink (turn-lifecycle.ts:361-374 drops them before sink.onEvent), so its later tool results are not passed; what it writes afterwards is opened by the end of the turn that superseded it, which took over its state. shown.end() is in a finally around the existing `await run`, which is the one site that runs for a turn that completed, failed, was stopped or was superseded. FOLLOWED TURN, in followLiveTurn (this window's own saved turn picked up after a window reload or a switch back to the chat, or one whose owner is gone): the presented turn is begun LAZILY, on the follow sink's first onEvent, never when the follow is asked for: followLiveTurn is asked for on every webview 'ready' (chat-panel.ts:691, 1436-1442) and turns.follow returns without following while this window runs the turn (turn-lifecycle.ts:403), so a request alone must not begin anything. toolResult is passed in the sink's onEvent the same way; end() is called in the sink's onEnd when the outcome is 'ended' and a turn was begun. A follow whose outcome is not 'ended' (a failed resume leaves the turn for a later follow) ends nothing. For a followed turn `before` is the list at its first event, so a document the turn wrote before the reload is not opened by the end rule (it is in the table); one it writes afterwards is. Each presenter call is wrapped so a throw is logged and the turn goes on.

errors.condition: A throwing presenter is caught and logged.

preconditions: None: with no presenter the host behaves as today
postconditions: The events posted to the chat's webview and the transcript rows are exactly as before
end() is called once per run turn, also when the turn failed, was stopped or was superseded
A message refused before any run begins no presented turn

api.name: DocsReviewHost.openArtifact (quiet), createPanel (quiet), ChatPanelChannel.reveal (preserveFocus)
api.signature: openArtifact(target: { artifactId: string; mdPath: string; quiet?: boolean | undefined }): void; createPanel(opts: { viewType: string; title: string; quiet?: boolean | undefined }): ChatPanelChannel; reveal(opts?: { preserveFocus?: boolean | undefined }): void

parameters.name: target.quiet
parameters.purpose: The pane is shown without taking keyboard focus. Absent or false: as today (the review command and the delivery board).

parameters.name: createPanel opts.quiet
parameters.purpose: The review host passes it on when it has to create the pane for a quiet open. extension.ts then creates the panel with { viewColumn: ViewColumn.Beside, preserveFocus: true }; without it, with ViewColumn.Active exactly as today.

parameters.name: reveal opts.preserveFocus
parameters.purpose: An optional argument on the shared channel interface. webview-channel.ts calls panel.reveal(undefined, true) when it is set and panel.reveal() otherwise, so every existing caller is unchanged.

returns.meaning: The host's open() gains an internal quiet argument: with no pane it calls createPanel({ viewType, title, quiet: true }); with a pane it calls channel.reveal({ preserveFocus: true }), so a pane that is a background tab is brought to the front of its group without moving the cursor out of the chat. The document is then opened with reveal as today, so the pane's document view shows it. The plugin's vscode.d.ts gains the two forms it does not declare yet: createWebviewPanel's showOptions as ViewColumn | { viewColumn: ViewColumn; preserveFocus?: boolean }, reveal(viewColumn?, preserveFocus?) and ViewColumn.Beside if absent. The reviewer's drafts on another document are kept, as they are saved per document.

errors.condition: A failed read of the document is shown in the pane as a failed open is today.

preconditions: The review host exists (the chat is enabled)
postconditions: The review command and the delivery board create the pane in the active column with focus and reveal it with focus, as before
A quiet open never moves keyboard focus

review-wiring.test.ts, which pins the source of the review host's createPanel in extension.ts (its lines 118-120 match `createPanel: ({ viewType, title }) => {` and the createWebviewPanel call with ViewColumn.Active), is restated in this Story: the non-quiet branch still creates with ViewColumn.Active and { enableScripts: true }; the quiet branch with { viewColumn: ViewColumn.Beside, preserveFocus: true }

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test run with tsx (npx tsx --test), as the plugin's chat tests are, with the fake channel, fake client and fake turn events those tests already use

migration.stateBefore: A document awaiting approval is shown in the review pane only when the user runs the review command and picks it, or opens it from the delivery board. The chat host passes tool results to its webview and transcript only.
migration.stateAfter: The chat host tells a presenter about each run turn's start, tool results and end; the presenter opens presented documents in the review pane, once per turn each, without taking focus.

migrationSteps.action: Add pendingDocuments() to the review client
Add the optional reveal argument to the channel, the quiet option to createPanel and openArtifact, and the two declarations to vscode.d.ts
Begin, feed and end a presented turn from the chat host's run turn and followed turn, and wire the presenter in extension.ts
Run the suite, build, package and install the plugin; check by hand

migration.backwardCompat: Plugin only. No daemon call, IPC shape or stored record changes. With no presenter wired the chat behaves exactly as before.

alternativesConsidered.name: A presenter fed by the chat turn: the tool result's path, and the pending list at the turn's end
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The chat host tells a small presenter about each tool result and the turn's end; the presenter opens what was presented, once per turn
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new module, review-presenter.ts, holds the rule. The chat host calls it at three points of a turn it runs: the start (the presenter reads the pending list and remembers which documents were already pending), each tool result (when the result's text is JSON carrying pendingApproval.artifactPath, the presenter re-reads the pending list and opens the pending document with that path), and the end (it re-reads the list and opens every document that became pending during the turn and was not opened yet in it). Opening goes through the review host's openArtifact with a new quiet flag, so the pane is created or updated without pulling keyboard focus from the chat. The client gains pendingDocuments() to give ids with paths.
pros: Covers a document written by a workflow tool call (seen at once, including a revision of a document that was already pending) and one produced any other way during the turn (seen at the turn's end): build and code review records, and workflows driven from a script
Plugin only; the daemon and its tool contract are unchanged
The rule is in one small module with no VS Code or webview dependency, so it is tested directly
Each document is opened once per turn; a re-read or re-render of the pane never calls the presenter
cons: Reads the pending list once at the start and end of every turn and once per presenting tool result
A document produced outside any chat turn (another terminal) is not opened

alternativesConsidered.name: Parse the tool result only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Open the document named by a tool result's pendingApproval block
alternativesConsidered.approach: The chat host looks for pendingApproval.artifactPath in each tool result and opens that path in the review pane.
cons: Misses every document that awaits approval without such a block: a build record, a code review record, and any workflow driven from a script inside the turn
Opens by path without knowing the artifact's id, so the pane cannot tell pending from read-only without another read anyway
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Simplest, but leaves out documents that are presented without the block.

alternativesConsidered.name: The review pane watches the pending list
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The pane's host polls the pending list and opens whatever is new
alternativesConsidered.approach: The review host polls workflow.pending on a timer (or watches .insrc/artifacts) and opens any new pending document, whether or not a chat turn made it.
pros: Also catches documents made outside the chat
cons: Opens documents the user was not presented with (another session's work, a batch of 200 code review records), which is not what was asked
A timer or a watch on a directory of several hundred files runs all the time
A revision of an already-pending document is not seen
The pane would have to exist before anything is presented
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Opens too much and at the wrong times.
